top_10_risks.title: Sample env disables destructive shell approval
Terminal response can run after mutating siblings
Resume claim and answer append are not atomic
DB-stored sidecar path can read arbitrary local file
Mixed URL+command MCP entries can bypass local-command trust blocking
Multi-user Web/API data is not consistently scoped to authenticated identity
Command hooks fail open by default
HTTP listener failure hidden by healthcheck

recommended_next_actions: Fix .env.example and shell destructive pattern parsing so copied sample configs preserve defaults.
Make terminal text_response exclusive with mutating or deferred sibling tools.
Fix single and batch pause resume atomicity.
Fence conversation sidecar reads by reconstructing paths from trusted IDs.
Reject ambiguous MCP server definitions that mix url and command, and require explicit runnable transport trust.
Scope AG-UI conversations and approvals by authenticated identity.
Default command hooks to fail-closed in production or require explicit fail policy.
Reject static object-store and Garage credentials outside development profiles.
Make AG-UI listener failure visible through readiness or process exit.
Introduce runtime profiles and a central ToolGateway policy layer.
